excerpts: In these methods and properties, you also define the logon type.
The logon type is defined by one of the constants in the TASK_LOGON_TYPE enumeration.
Tasks registered with the TASK_LOGON_PASSWORD or TASK_LOGON_S4U flag will only launch if the specified user has the Logon as Batch privilege enabled.
This is important to consider when registering tasks with an interactive logon type.

When you register a task with the logon type equal to TASK_LOGON_INTERACTIVE_TOKEN and the task does not have credentials specified in the Principal property of the task definition, specified in the parameters to RegisterTaskDefinition , or specified in the XML that is passed to RegisterTask , then the task will be registered with the credentials of the user that called the Connect method.

Tasks can specify that they will run with elevated privileges or low privileges by setting a privilege level from the TASK_RUNLEVEL_TYPE enumeration for the RunLevel property of IPrincipal ( Principal.RunLevel for scripting).
The value of the RunLevel property determines the privilege level at which a task's actions will be run.
If a task's actions must have elevated privileges to run, then you must set the RunLevel property to TASK_RUNLEVEL_HIGHEST .
If a task is registered using the Administrators group for the security context of the task, then you must also set the RunLevel property to TASK_RUNLEVEL_HIGHEST if you want to run the task.
If a task is registered using the Builtin\Administrator account or the Local System or Local Service accounts, then the RunLevel property will be ignored.

This constant cannot be combined with the TASK_CREATE , TASK_UPDATE , or TASK_CREATE_OR_UPDATE values.
TASK_CREATE 0x2 The Task Scheduler registers the task as a new task.
TASK_CREATE_OR_UPDATE 0x6 The Task Scheduler either registers the task as a new task or as an updated version if the task already exists.
Equivalent to TASK_CREATE | TASK_UPDATE.
When the TASK_LOGON_SERVICE_ACCOUNT logon type is used, the password must be an empty VARIANT value such as VT_NULL or VT_EMPTY .
logonType [in] Defines what logon technique is used to run the registered task.
Value Meaning TASK_LOGON_NONE 0 The logon method is not specified.
TASK_LOGON_PASSWORD 1 Use a password for logging on the user.
Logon Trigger Example (Scripting) Feedback Summarize this article for me In this article This scripting example shows how to create a task that is scheduled to execute Notepad when a user logs on.
The task contains a logon trigger that specifies a start boundary for the task to start and a user identifier that specifies the user.
Create a logon trigger using the TaskDefinition.Triggers property.
Use the TriggerCollection.Create method (specifying the type of trigger that you want to create) to create a logon trigger.
const TriggerTypeLogon = 9 ' A constant that specifies an executable action.
Dim settings Set settings = taskDefinition.Settings settings.StartWhenAvailable = True '******************************************************** ' Create a logon trigger.
Dim triggers Set triggers = taskDefinition.Triggers Dim trigger Set trigger = triggers.Create(TriggerTypeLogon) ' Trigger variables that define when the trigger is active.

Dim startTime, endTime startTime = "2006-05-02T10:49:02" endTime = "2006-05-02T10:52:02" WScript.Echo "startTime :" & startTime WScript.Echo "endTime :" & endTime trigger.StartBoundary = startTime trigger.EndBoundary = endTime trigger.ExecutionTimeLimit = "PT5M" ' Five minutes trigger.Id = "LogonTriggerId" trigger.UserId = "DOMAIN\UserName" ' Must be a valid user account '*********************************************************** ' Create the action for the task to execute.

const createOrUpdateTask = 6 call rootFolder.RegisterTaskDefinition( _ "Test Logon Trigger", taskDefinition, createOrUpdateTask, _ "Builtin\Administrators", , 4) WScript.Echo "Task submitted." Related topics Using the Task Scheduler Feedback Was this page helpful?

Get Installed Voices Method Definition Namespace: System.Speech.Synthesis Assembly: System.Speech.dll Package: System.Speech v11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 Important Some information relates to prerelease product that may be substantially modified before it’s released.
Returns the collection of speech synthesis (text-to-speech) voices that are currently installed on the system.
Overloads Name Description GetInstalledVoices() Returns all of the installed speech synthesis (text-to-speech) voices.
GetInstalledVoices(CultureInfo) Returns all of the installed speech synthesis (text-to-speech) voices that support a specific locale.
Remarks When an application calls GetInstalledVoices , the method verifies that each of the voices (engines for text-to-speech) it finds in the registry meets certain minimum criteria.
For any voice that fails verification, GetInstalledVoices sets its Enabled property to False .
